pr_title: Add header dictionary analyzer and fixer
pr_comments:
Brought in changes from https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/44061 so I can get all tests to pass when I update the verifiers.

It's merged in release/7.0, and will get merged to main soon. Small merge conflict to resolve depending on who gets merged first 💪

issue_context.title: Add an Analyzer to recommend using DIM properties with IHeaderDictionary instead of indexer
comments:
Thanks for contacting us.

We're moving this issue to the `.NET 8 Planning` milestone for future evaluation / consideration. We would like to keep this around to collect more feedback, which can help us with prioritizing this work. We will re-evaluate this issue, during our next planning meeting(s). 
If we later determine, that the issue has no community involvement, or it's very rare and low-impact issue, we will close it - so that the team can focus on more important and high impact issues.
To learn more about what to expect next and how this issue will be handled you can read more about our triage process [here](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/docs/TriageProcess.md).

review_comments:
I like this pattern for checking the fully-qualified type of a symbol. It's a lot better than what we're currently doing in another analyzer:

https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/8ce81e9dac0db17415dd21eea4f02ce025f3924c/src/Framework/AspNetCoreAnalyzers/src/Analyzers/RouteHandlers/DetectMisplacedLambdaAttribute.cs#L61-L74
Yeah, it's a fun syntax. The downside is it's tough to debug when it doesn't work. Can't step through it 😢

Can you open a matching issue on AspNetCore.Docs to track adding the documentation for this?

I think we should try to be proactive about documenting analyzers as we implement them for .NET 8 so we don't find ourselves having to write docs for multiple analyzes at the end of a release (like we are now 😅 ).

Non-blocking feedback: while we're making changes here, do you mind deleting the other verifiers in this directory and updating all the tests to use this one? I realized that with our test setup there was no need for us to have a verifier per analyzer type.
For thoroughness, can we add a test that verifies the analyzers don't emit diagnostics for references that already use DIM properties?
